test.name: With no project, finds five census heads by name, reads them, and links each page and the records on it
test.description: Issue #4583, the tester's shape. Direct-agent arm in an empty folder, with no projectPath. An earlier report named the 1825 Lower Canada census heads of Hemmingford with no links; the researcher then asked: "Cite the sources for the 1825 census entries for Hemmingford, including the specific images available on FamilySearch." The router hands search-records that message with the collection, the place and five heads by name. Step 7b: the agent finds each head with record_search (no projectPath), reads each with record_read (no projectPath), and after its final `---` gives one line per page, the page linked by its viewerUrl and the records on it linked by their recordUrl, and cites the collection once. Three pages: 3:1:9396-MWWN-1 holds William Brisbin, Joseph Brisbin and Hugh Emerson; 3:1:9396-MWWB-Q holds Elisha Calkins; 3:1:9396-MWWB-8 holds Ashal Calkins. With no project it writes nothing. The searches and reads are live captures (2026-11-17), in the shape the tester's own search-records sent.

input.delegation:
There is no project; there is no projectPath. The researcher wrote:

Cite the sources for the 1825 census entries for Hemmingford, including the specific images available on FamilySearch.

Collection: Canada, Lower Canada, Census, 1825. Place: Hemmingford, Huntingdon, Quebec, Canada. Records found earlier, by name, with no links given: William Brisbin, Joseph Brisbin, Hugh Emerson, Elisha Calkins, Ashal Calkins.

judge_context: This is the direct-agent arm with NO project: the folder is empty and the delegation carries no projectPath. The agent searches and reads with no projectPath. Logging is NOT expected: a research_log_append, research_append or extraction_append call, or any call carrying a projectPath, is a fault, not thoroughness. Saying plainly that nothing was saved is correct.

Searches by surname in collection 1834346 (Canada, Lower Canada, Census, 1825) at Hemmingford return the heads: Brisbin gives William (ark:/61903/1:1:KHJ8-J56) and Joseph (ark:/61903/1:1:KHJ8-J5Z); Emerson gives Hugh (ark:/61903/1:1:KHJ8-J5C) and a second Emerson head the researcher did not name, who need not be read or reported; Calkins gives Elisha (ark:/61903/1:1:KHJ8-JTQ) and Ashal (ark:/61903/1:1:KHJ8-V9Y). Any other search returns nothing. A search per head instead of per surname is fine.

The record_read answers give three pages. https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:9396-MWWN-1 holds William Brisbin (record https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:2:9MFD-5SJP), Joseph Brisbin (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:2:9MFD-5SJ2) and Hugh Emerson (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:2:9MFD-5SJK). https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:9396-MWWB-Q holds Elisha Calkins (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:2:9MFD-5SKX). https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:9396-MWWB-8 holds Ashal Calkins (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:2:9MFD-5SR4). The collection is "Canada, Lower Canada, Census, 1825" (FamilySearch's own citation names it "Canada, recensement du Bas-Canada, 1825").

PASS requires, after the agent's final `---` line: one line per page, the page as a markdown link to its viewerUrl, then the heads on that page, each as a markdown link to its recordUrl, every page and head above present and on the right page, and the collection cited once. A page or a head that is missing, put on the wrong page, or given as a bare ARK or a link the tool answers did not give, is a fail; so is stopping after the searches without reading the records. A deterministic validator (gives-record-image-links) checks that every link the reads gave is present; grade the grouping and the citation.

The block after `---` MAY carry these links: the agent's return contract allows the links Step 7b gives in place of the usual plain-prose first paragraph. Do not mark it down for identifiers or for being a list.
